title: John Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on John chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: John Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of John Chapter 13.

questions.question: In John 13, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Judas Iscariot was put in the heart by the devil to betray Jesus
Jesus knew his hour was come to depart out of this world unto the Father
Simon Peter refused to have his feet washed
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus knew his hour was come to depart out of this world unto the Father
questions.explanation: John 13:1 states that Jesus knew his hour was come before the feast of the passover, which is the earliest event mentioned

questions.question: Who did the devil put into the heart to betray Jesus?
questions.explanation: John 13:2 states the devil put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon's son, to betray Jesus

questions.question: What did Jesus do after supper ended?
options: He laid aside his garments and took a towel to gird himself
He went to pray in the garden
questions.correctAnswer: He laid aside his garments and took a towel to gird himself
questions.explanation: John 13:4 records that Jesus rose from supper, laid aside his garments, and took a towel and girded himself

questions.question: What did Jesus do with the water he poured into a basin?
options: He washed the disciples' feet and wiped them with a towel
He used it to clean the table
questions.correctAnswer: He washed the disciples' feet and wiped them with a towel
questions.explanation: John 13:5 states Jesus poured water into a basin and began to wash the disciples' feet and wipe them with the towel

questions.question: Who did Jesus come to first to wash feet?
questions.explanation: John 13:6 says Jesus came to Simon Peter first when washing the disciples' feet

questions.question: What was Peter's initial reaction when Jesus came to wash his feet?
options: He said, 'Lord, dost thou wash my feet?'
questions.correctAnswer: He said, 'Lord, dost thou wash my feet?'
questions.explanation: John 13:6 records Peter's question to Jesus asking if He would wash his feet

questions.question: What did Jesus say to Peter when Peter objected to having his feet washed?
options: If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me
questions.correctAnswer: If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me
questions.explanation: John 13:8 quotes Jesus telling Peter that unless He washes him, he has no part with Him

questions.question: What did Peter ask Jesus to wash after his feet?
questions.explanation: John 13:9 shows Peter asking Jesus to wash not only his feet but also his hands and head

questions.question: According to Jesus, who needs only to have their feet washed because they are clean overall?
questions.explanation: John 13:10 states that he who is washed needs only to have his feet washed because he is clean every whit

questions.question: Why did Jesus say, 'Ye are not all clean'?
options: Because he knew who should betray him
Because they had not washed their hands
questions.correctAnswer: Because he knew who should betray him
questions.explanation: John 13:11 explains that Jesus said this because he knew who would betray him

questions.question: What did Jesus do after washing the disciples' feet and taking his garments?
options: Sat down and asked if they knew what he had done
questions.correctAnswer: Sat down and asked if they knew what he had done
questions.explanation: John 13:12 states Jesus sat down again and asked the disciples if they knew what he had done

questions.question: True or False: Jesus was called Master and Lord by the disciples, and He affirmed this title.
questions.explanation: John 13:13 states the disciples call Jesus Master and Lord and He says well, for so He is

questions.question: True or False: Jesus knew that the Father had given all things into his hands.
questions.explanation: John 13:3 explicitly states Jesus knew the Father had given all things into His hands

questions.question: True or False: Jesus immediately explained to Peter why He was washing his feet.
questions.explanation: John 13:7 shows Jesus said Peter did not know now what He was doing but would know later, so the explanation was not immediate

questions.question: True or False: Jesus washed the whole body of each disciple during supper.
questions.explanation: John 13:5-10 indicates Jesus washed the disciples' feet, not their entire bodies

medium.title: John Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from John Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What example did Jesus give to his disciples in John 13?
questions.explanation: Jesus said, 'If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another's feet.' (John 13:14)

questions.question: What does John 13:17 promise will happen if someone does what John 13:15 commands?
questions.explanation: John 13:17 states, 'If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.' This reflects the promise of happiness in obedience to Jesus' example.

questions.question: According to John 13:16, who is not greater than his lord?
questions.explanation: Jesus declared, 'The servant is not greater than his lord; neither he that is sent greater than he that sent him.' (John 13:16)

questions.question: How did the disciples react to Jesus' statement about betrayal in John 13:21?
options: They looked at each other, doubting
questions.correctAnswer: They looked at each other, doubting
questions.explanation: The disciples were confused and looked at one another, as stated in John 13:22: 'Then the disciples looked one on another, doubting of whom he spake.'

questions.question: What did Jesus do before washing the disciples' feet, according to John 13:4?
questions.explanation: John 13:4 states, 'He riseth from supper, and laid aside his garments; and took a towel, and girded himself.' This act signifies His humility and service.

questions.question: What did Jesus mean when He said in John 13:18 that 'He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me'?
options: He will establish a new covenant
questions.explanation: This statement refers to Judas Iscariot's betrayal, fulfilling the scripture as indicated in John 13:18.

questions.question: What does John 13:19 indicate Jesus is doing by telling His disciples about the betrayal beforehand?
questions.explanation: By predicting the betrayal, Jesus aims for His disciples to believe that He is the Messiah, as stated in John 13:19.

questions.question: According to John 13:20, what is the relationship between receiving those whom Jesus sends and receiving Jesus Himself?
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes the unity of mission in John 13:20: 'He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me.'

questions.question: What does the act of washing feet symbolize in the context of John 13?
questions.explanation: Jesus' act of washing the disciples' feet symbolizes the service and humility expected of His followers, as seen in John 13:14.

questions.question: In John 13:10, who did Jesus say was clean?
questions.explanation: Jesus indicates that 'ye are clean, but not all,' referring to the disciples but acknowledging Judas' unclean heart (John 13:10).

questions.question: What does John 13:15 encourage followers of Jesus to do?
questions.explanation: Jesus states in John 13:15, 'For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you,' urging them to emulate His actions.

questions.question: In John 13:11, why did Jesus say, 'Ye are not all clean'?
options: He was referring to their actions
He knew Judas would betray Him
He wanted to teach a lesson
questions.correctAnswer: He knew Judas would betray Him
questions.explanation: Jesus knew the heart of Judas Iscariot, which is why He said, 'Ye are not all clean' (John 13:11).

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus washed the feet of all His disciples?
questions.explanation: Jesus washed the feet of all His disciples as an act of service, demonstrating humility and love.

questions.question: Is it false that Jesus only chose certain disciples to send out in His ministry?
questions.explanation: Jesus sent His disciples out to spread the gospel broadly, as seen in John 13:20, meaning He did not choose only certain ones.

questions.question: Is it false that Peter immediately accepted Jesus' foot washing?
questions.explanation: Peter initially resisted Jesus' washing of his feet, indicating his misunderstanding of the significance of the act (John 13:8).

hard.title: John Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from John Chapter 13.

questions.question: According to John 13:27, who entered into Judas after Jesus gave him the sop?
questions.explanation: John 13:27 explicitly states 'And after the sop Satan entered into him.'

questions.question: What was the reaction of those at the table to Jesus’ words to Judas in John 13:28?
options: They did not understand his intent
They immediately knew Judas would betray Him
questions.correctAnswer: They did not understand his intent
questions.explanation: John 13:28 says, 'Now no man at the table knew for what intent he spake this unto him,' showing they were unaware of Jesus' meaning.

questions.question: Why did some at the table think Jesus spoke to Judas about buying things or giving to the poor (John 13:29)?
questions.explanation: John 13:29 states, 'For some of them thought, because Judas had the bag, that Jesus had said unto him, Buy those things… or give something to the poor.'

questions.question: What time of day was it when Judas left after receiving the sop in John 13:30?
questions.explanation: John 13:30 concludes with 'He then having received the sop went immediately out: and it was night.'

questions.question: What does Jesus say is glorified when Judas leaves, according to John 13:31?
options: The Son of man and God
questions.correctAnswer: The Son of man and God
questions.explanation: John 13:31 states, 'Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him.'

questions.question: What new commandment does Jesus give in John 13:34?
options: That ye love one another as I have loved you
That ye keep the law strictly
That ye fast twice a week
questions.correctAnswer: That ye love one another as I have loved you
questions.explanation: John 13:34 says, 'A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you…'

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'sop' (John 13:26) mean?
questions.explanation: In John 13:26, 'sop' (Greek: 'dipsa') refers to a piece of bread dipped in sauce or broth, a common cultural practice during meals.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in John 13:34-35 regarding love?
questions.explanation: John 13:34-35 uses inclusio by framing the passage with the theme of love to enclose the teaching, emphasizing its importance.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed in Jesus’ statement about betrayal in John 13:18?
questions.explanation: John 13:18 cites Psalm 41:9, 'He that eateth bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me,' referring to betrayal by a close companion.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage parallels Jesus’ new commandment to love one another in John 13:34?
questions.explanation: 1 John 4:7-8 emphasizes love as essential to knowing God, paralleling the commandment in John 13:34 to love one another.

questions.question: What action immediately precedes Jesus giving the new commandment in John 13:34?
questions.explanation: John 13:31-33 describe Judas leaving and Jesus speaking of being glorified, immediately preceding the new commandment in verse 34.

questions.question: What typology is represented by Jesus washing the disciples’ feet in John 13:4-5?
questions.explanation: Jesus washing feet (John 13:4-5) symbolizes servant leadership, contrasting worldly power with humble service.

questions.question: What foreshadowing is present in Jesus’ dialogue with Peter in John 13:38?
options: Peter’s denial before the cock crows
The coming of the Holy Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: Peter’s denial before the cock crows
questions.explanation: John 13:38 predicts Peter’s denial three times before the cock crows, foreshadowing his failure despite good intentions.

questions.question: How does John 13:27-30 create an inclusio with Judas’ betrayal?
options: By beginning and ending with Judas receiving the sop
questions.correctAnswer: By beginning and ending with Judas receiving the sop
questions.explanation: John 13:26-30 frames Judas’ betrayal with the giving and receiving of the sop, forming an inclusio highlighting betrayal.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus says in John 13:36 that Peter can follow Him now.
questions.explanation: John 13:36 records Jesus telling Peter, 'Whither I go, thou canst not follow me now; but thou shalt follow me afterwards.'

theological.title: John Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from John Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does John 13:1 teach about Jesus’ love in relation to salvation?
options: Jesus’ love is unconditional and persevering until the end
Jesus loves only those who are sinless
Jesus’ love is temporary and conditional
Jesus loves only during his earthly ministry
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus’ love is unconditional and persevering until the end
questions.explanation: John 13:1 states that Jesus loved his own which were in the world, and he loved them unto the end, indicating the doctrine of persevering and unconditional love.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine foreknowledge and human sinfulness is taught in John 13:11?
options: Jesus knew the identity of the betrayer, demonstrating divine foreknowledge
Jesus was ignorant of Judas’ betrayal until after it happened
The disciples had full knowledge of Judas’ sin beforehand
Jesus did not know who would betray him
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus knew the identity of the betrayer, demonstrating divine foreknowledge
questions.explanation: John 13:11 says Jesus knew who should betray him, which demonstrates the doctrine of divine foreknowledge coexisting with human sinfulness.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification is taught in John 13:10?
options: Sanctification involves ongoing cleansing from sin, symbolized by washing feet
Once saved, no further cleansing is needed
Sanctification is only external and ceremonial
Only priests need to be sanctified
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves ongoing cleansing from sin, symbolized by washing feet
questions.explanation: John 13:10 explains that those washed need only to have their feet washed, symbolizing ongoing sanctification through cleansing from daily sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does John 13:3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: John 13:3 shows Jesus knowing that the Father had given all things into his hands and that he came from God and was going to God, demonstrating divine omniscience.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is illustrated in John 13:27 when Satan enters Judas after receiving the sop?
questions.explanation: Jesus’ command to Judas to do quickly what he must do in John 13:27 shows God’s sovereignty over even evil actions.

questions.question: How does the foot-washing episode in John 13:4-5 connect to Old Testament typology of priestly service?
options: It fulfills the priestly role by demonstrating humble service as in Exodus 30:18-21
It rejects all Old Testament ceremonial laws
It shows Jesus acting as a warrior king
It connects to the temple sacrifices exclusively
questions.correctAnswer: It fulfills the priestly role by demonstrating humble service as in Exodus 30:18-21
questions.explanation: Jesus girding himself to wash feet in John 13:4-5 echoes the priestly duties of ceremonial cleansing in Exodus, symbolizing humble service.

questions.question: In what way does John 13:34-35 prepare for the eschatological community described in 1 John 4:7-8?
options: By commanding love among believers as the identifying mark of discipleship
By emphasizing ritual purity over love
By focusing solely on obedience to law
questions.correctAnswer: By commanding love among believers as the identifying mark of discipleship
questions.explanation: John 13:34-35 commands love as the new commandment, which is the basis for the community of love described in 1 John 4:7-8.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do John 13:7 and John 13:19 teach about Jesus’ revelation and messianic identity?
options: Jesus reveals his identity progressively and foretells his betrayal to strengthen faith
Jesus hides his identity completely until after the resurrection
Jesus denies any messianic role to avoid conflict
Jesus reveals all mysteries immediately and openly
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus reveals his identity progressively and foretells his betrayal to strengthen faith
questions.explanation: John 13:7 speaks of future understanding of Jesus’ actions, and John 13:19 predicts the betrayal so disciples may believe, showing gradual revelation of his messianic identity.

questions.question: What doctrinal synthesis about judgment and election is taught in John 13:11 and John 13:18?
options: Jesus knows the elect and foretells the fulfillment of Scripture regarding betrayal
Jesus is unaware of who will betray him
Election is not connected to Scripture in this chapter
Judgment is delayed until after the resurrection only
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus knows the elect and foretells the fulfillment of Scripture regarding betrayal
questions.explanation: John 13:11 states Jesus knew who would betray him, and John 13:18 cites Scripture’s fulfillment about the betrayal, linking divine election and judgment.

questions.question: What do John 13:14 and John 13:15 together teach about Christian humility and service?
options: Believers are called to imitate Jesus’ humble foot washing as a model for servant leadership
Service is only for clergy, not laity
Jesus’ foot washing was symbolic but not normative
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to imitate Jesus’ humble foot washing as a model for servant leadership
questions.explanation: John 13:14 commands believers to wash one another’s feet and 13:15 says Jesus gave an example to follow, teaching servant leadership humility.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Jesus’ foot washing in John 13:4-10 undermines his divine majesty. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Jesus demonstrates divine humility and servant leadership without diminishing his majesty
Jesus temporarily gave up his divinity to wash feet
Jesus’ act was a concession to cultural norms only
Jesus’ majesty is compromised by this act
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus demonstrates divine humility and servant leadership without diminishing his majesty
questions.explanation: John 13:4-10 shows Jesus, fully divine, humbling himself to serve, illustrating that divine majesty includes humility, not diminishment.

questions.question: What doctrine about the unity of the Godhead is taught in John 13:20?
options: Receiving Jesus’ messengers is equivalent to receiving both Jesus and the Father
The Father and Son act independently without unity
Jesus sends no one on God’s behalf
Only the Father is to be received, not the Son
questions.correctAnswer: Receiving Jesus’ messengers is equivalent to receiving both Jesus and the Father
questions.explanation: John 13:20 teaches that receiving those Jesus sends is receiving Jesus, and receiving Jesus is receiving the Father, demonstrating Trinitarian unity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Jesus’ knowledge of Judas’ betrayal in John 13:21?
questions.explanation: Jesus being troubled in spirit yet knowing the betrayal in John 13:21 reveals his omniscience regarding future events.

questions.question: What narrative-historical function does Judas’ departure in John 13:30 serve in the Gospel’s passion narrative?
options: It initiates the betrayal event leading to Jesus’ arrest and crucifixion
It marks Judas’ repentance and restoration
It interrupts the meal without further significance
questions.correctAnswer: It initiates the betrayal event leading to Jesus’ arrest and crucifixion
questions.explanation: John 13:30 shows Judas immediately leaving after receiving the sop, precipitating the fulfillment of the passion narrative.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about discipleship and perseverance is taught in John 13:36-38?
options: True discipleship includes enduring trials and possible denial before ultimate following
Discipleship guarantees no failure or denial
Peter’s declaration ensures he will not fail
Following Jesus is purely optional without cost
questions.correctAnswer: True discipleship includes enduring trials and possible denial before ultimate following
questions.explanation: Jesus predicts Peter’s denial in John 13:38, teaching that discipleship involves perseverance despite failure or weakness.
